finding: A SPLITSHARD that fails because the parent-leader node is stopped right after CREATESHARD leaves sub-shard shard1_0 in CONSTRUCTION in state.json for good (SplitShardCmd does no rollback), so waitForRecoveriesToFinish sees a CONSTRUCTION slice on every poll and times out at AbstractDistribZkTestBase.java:185.
same_root_cause: No. The agent's failure comes from SplitShardCmd (solr/core/src/java/org/apache/solr/cloud/SplitShardCmd.java:266 creates the sub-shard as CONSTRUCTION; the later addReplica at :298 throws 'At least one of the node(s) specified are not currently active' and the command rethrows with no cleanup). The CONSTRUCTION slice really is in ZooKeeper: the printLayoutToStdOut dump in logs/validate-1.log (around line 4099) shows "state":"construction" in state.json. So the client is not seeing stale cached state. SOLR-9440's defect is in ZkStateReader.removeCollectionStateWatcher (solr/solrj/.../ZkStateReader.java, hunk @@ -1340): when the last watcher is removed, the entry is dropped from collectionWatches but the DocCollection stays in watchedCollectionStates and is never replaced by a LazyCollectionRef, so the client's ClusterState stays frozen. The fix adds watchedCollectionStates.remove, lazyCollectionStates.put(new LazyCollectionRef) and constructState. The agent's test never relies on a watcher being removed and then on the client's view going stale; its waitForState calls only feed correct data.
realistic: Yes, as a trigger for its own bug: an ordinary async SPLITSHARD plus stopping and restarting a node with ChaosMonkey in a MiniSolrCloudCluster. The TestInjection core-creation delay never fired. It is a plausible different bug (no cleanup of sub-shards after a failed split, which later Solr versions addressed), not SOLR-9440.
fixed_version: Still reproduces on the fixed tree: logs/validate-fixed-1.log shows shard1_0 state=construction and the same AssertionError at AbstractDistribZkTestBase.java:185. That fits a defect the SOLR-9440 fix does not touch, and this fix prevents the stale state rather than handling the exception.
reason: The check fails because a failed split leaves a real CONSTRUCTION slice in ZooKeeper, not because ZkStateReader serves a stale cached DocCollection after removeCollectionStateWatcher. The root cause is in SplitShardCmd's missing failure cleanup, which the SOLR-9440 fix does not change, and the failure persists on the fixed version. So it does not detect SOLR-9440.
